card.name: Dose-related words before a unit or limit
card.fires_on: Dose-related spots in drug labels: an opening parenthesis after "Dose", the unit "mg" after a number, or words like "dose" and "levels" in sentences about amounts. It is also seen on "low" or "a" before a property word.

modes.label: Parenthesis after Dose
modes.description: An opening bracket right after the word Dose in a table or formula, just before the unit.
modes.example: CALVERT FORMULA FOR CARBOPLATIN DOSING Total Dose<< (>>mg) = (target AUC)

modes.label: mg after a number
modes.description: The unit mg following a dose number, in dosing limits or titration steps.
modes.example: Dosage above 100<< mg>> daily usually does not increase effectiveness.

modes.label: dose or levels as a noun
modes.description: The word dose or levels in a sentence about how much of a drug is involved.

card.plain: It marks spots in dose text where a unit or amount comes next, and it rules out the word density.
